title: Records
objectives: Use records for immutable data carriers

sections.markdown: A record (Java 16+) is a concise, immutable data carrier. The compiler generates the constructor, private final fields, accessors, equals, hashCode and toString for you.
Expecting to mutate a record or extend it — records are final and their fields are final. Use them for immutable values (DTOs, keys), not entities you mutate.
Records pair beautifully with sealed types + pattern matching for modeling closed data hierarchies — the basis of algebraic data types in Java.

flashcards.back: Constructor, private final fields, accessors, equals, hashCode, and toString.

flashcards.front: Can a record be mutable or extended?
flashcards.back: No — records are final with final fields; designed for immutable data.
A record constructor body for validation/normalization without listing parameters.
